title: Read template processing and recursive list helpers
description: You follow the supplied Python simulation and its list-processing examples.
source: draft: codex free model + edit: codex

steps.description: You process a template by checking marker cases before ordinary nested lists. Environment lookups supply marked values, and unmarked items remain in the resulting structure.
You run the two supplied templates with their environments. The recording prints [define,Alice,42] and [my-func,1,2,3] as their resulting lists.
You define first-element, remaining-list, and prepend helpers. The recursive map and filter functions stop at an empty list.

steps.question: What does my_reduce return when its remaining list becomes empty?
steps.answer: It returns init, the accumulator passed into that call. Each preceding call supplied f(init,car(lst)) as the next accumulator.

steps.description: You see the squares, evens [2,4], and sum 15 for the supplied list. The final composed calculation prints 20.
